notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Reproduced against d4a2c8d: 12 completed TestJobManager jobs, queue {limit:1,running:0,queued:0}, and 12 open test-log descriptors. Fixture state and files were removed. Source: src/server/log-writer.ts:69-110 and src/server/test-job-manager.ts:239-247. Missing disk retention is established by inspection of SqliteStateStore.saveTestRun and FileLogWriter, not a disk-growth benchmark.

problem: FileLogWriter retains a WriteStream in testFiles for every run until controller shutdown. Finishing a test does not close or remove it.
SQLite keeps a bounded completed-run history, but deleting historical run records does not remove their corresponding log files. Per-file rotation does not bound total test-log storage.

risk.rollback: Disable new retention deletion if its ownership checks fail while keeping per-run log closure. Preserve active/retained logs; already expired logs cannot be reconstructed after deletion.

scope: Add an explicit per-run log finalization path and call it exactly once on success, failure, cancellation, timeout, and spawn error. Flush final output, close the descriptor, and remove the writer from memory.

Align completed test-log retention with retained run history, including rotated files, without deleting active or queued output. Define cleanup after project removal and interrupted-controller recovery.
Keep any cleanup restricted to controller-owned log names under the configured log root. Surface write/close failures without turning a failed verification into a success.
source: Repository assessment and owner direction on 2026-09-05
title: Close completed test logs and bound their retained resources
validation: Run a sequence of short jobs in an isolated controller state directory. Open test-log descriptors and writer entries must return to a bounded baseline after completion; Linux can verify /proc/self/fd.
Exceed the configured completed-run retention and verify obsolete logs and rotated copies are removed while retained and active run output remains readable.
Verify final output survives finish/close races, repeated finalization is harmless, and shutdown does not reopen completed log streams.
value: The persistent controller can run for weeks without accumulating one open file and retained log set per verification.
